model: REIT operating profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; funds management plus IAS 40 co-investments)
model_label: Operating Earnings FCFE DCF at AUD cost of equity, component-built, LTIP charged in the flows, retained-earnings reinvestment charged as capex; hybrid of the REIT/distributable-profit row and the operating-company engine (CHC.AX precedent)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 operating EPS guidance (+9.0%, FY26 results 19 Aug 2026), used for year 1; the 10-year path fades from it toward 3% terminal
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (13.6%) diverges >30% from statutory EPS 5yr CAGR (1.7%) and both statutory series are unusable as growth reads: statutory EPS peaked on FY21-22 revaluation gains (1.221, 1.788) and went negative in FY24 (-0.052), while book equity compounds on the same fair-value marks plus retained earnings. Statutory revenue (9.2%/5.2%) excludes the equity-accounted Partnership share of earnings that is most of the growth. Operating EPS (11.0%/14.5%) is the only clean series and it is management's own measure; the selected 9.0% is management's FY27 guidance on it, below every historical rate.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr are computed on Operating Profit (FY21 1,219.4 -> FY23 1,783.2 -> FY26 2,674.5), Goodman's distributable measure, because reported FCF is not an owner flow here (capex in the CSV is corporate PP&E only; the real deployment runs through investment properties, inventories and Partnership equity). Operating Profit is pre-LTIP; the after-LTIP (house) series grew faster over 5 years (18.4% vs 17.0%) because the LTIP was 22% of Operating Profit in FY21 and 17% in FY26, and slower over 3 years (13.8% vs 14.5%) because the FY26 charge jumped 31%. Distribution per security has been 30.0c since FY19 (payout fell from 56% to 23%), so the DPS CAGR says nothing about earnings.

scenario_narratives.base: Goodman delivers FY27 guidance (operating EPS +9%, distribution held at 30c) and compounds Operating Profit at 9% through FY29 as the data-centre WIP reaches ready-for-service in CY2028 and Partnership AUM grows, then fades to 3% by FY36. Roughly two-thirds of Operating Profit continues to be retained and deployed into development and co-investment at a 14% incremental return, so free cash to securityholders starts near the distribution and rises as reinvestment needs fade. The LTIP is treated as the real cost it is (house basis), which takes ~17% off Goodman's own Operating Profit. The axes that matter are data-centre leasing conversion (25% pre-commitment on A$19.7bn WIP), the availability of third-party capital to keep the own-develop-manage model capital-light, and whether retained capital keeps earning well above the 10% cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-centre pivot works at scale: the 0.5GW in WIP and the 6.4GW power bank convert into long-dated hyperscale leases (the TYO05 20-year, 50MW lease repeated across Sydney, Tokyo, Frankfurt, LA and the DataBank JV), development earnings step up as CY2028 RFS dates land, AUM and base fees follow, and capital Partners keep funding the pipeline. Operating earnings grow 10-14% for four years and the LTIP charge moderates as the plan is simplified. Retained capital earns ~18%, close to the FY16-FY26 record. Value is capped at a 20x terminal multiple on free cash to equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The speculative development book meets a cooler AI-infrastructure market: hyperscaler capex slows, community and grid constraints delay or cancel projects, the 75% uncommitted share of WIP leases slowly at lower rents, performance fees stay at zero, cap rates widen and the FY26-style realisation of prior revaluation gains stops. Development earnings fall ~30% over FY28-FY30, the platform's sticky costs compress the margin ~6pp, and retained capital earns only its cost. Rent from the 95.6%-occupied logistics book and 6.5% gearing keep this an earnings-and-multiple case, not a survival case; the trough is ~6.5% below FY26 Operating earnings, followed by a 3% recovery trend.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Goodman is valued on the flow it actually generates for securityholders, Operating Profit, discounted at the AUD cost of equity with no separate debt deduction (the flow is already after balance-sheet and Partnership-level interest). Two adjustments separate this from Goodman's own framing: the A$465.8m LTIP expense is charged in the flows, because Operating Profit excludes it and the Board's dilution-based offset covers only rights already tested; and the two-thirds of Operating Profit that is retained to fund development is charged as reinvestment, so the guided 9% growth is paid for rather than free. Together these are why the house value sits well below the 20x operating-EPS multiple the market is paying: a model that capitalises all of Operating Profit as free cash at the same rate would value the group roughly 2-3x higher. The street basis (LTIP as non-cash) is reported alongside and is the better comparison to sell-side targets; the sum-of-parts memo (NTA A$11.79 + management platform A$2.4 + development franchise A$2-4) brackets A$16-18 and corroborates the street base. The market price implies the data-centre pipeline leases at scale and retained capital keeps earning close to its historical ~20%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Incremental return on retained capital is the single largest lever: the base assumes 14% (FY26 Operating Profit on book equity 11.1%; FY16-FY26 incremental ~20%). At 18% the house base rises toward the bull value; at 10% retention creates no value and the base falls toward the bear.

LTIP treatment: charging the accounting expense (14.5% of Operating earnings, up 31% in FY26) rather than the dilution the Board points to is the house rule; the street values show what the valuation looks like on Goodman's own definition. The FY27 plan simplification may cut the charge faster than the modelled 0.5pp/yr glide.

FY26 Operating Profit includes 733.7 of realised prior-year revaluation gains (FY25 253.3); the base takes FY27 guidance at face value, which requires further large realisations. If transfers into Partnerships slow, year-1 growth disappoints even before the data-centre leasing question is answered.

Discount rate: value is terminal-heavy at a 10% cost of equity (Gordon 14.7x FCFE binds in base); each 1pp on the rate moves the base ~15%. The required-return table shows what the current price implies.

Data-centre execution: 78% of A$19.7bn WIP with 25% pre-commitment and first RFS mostly CY2028; leasing outcomes, grid connection delays (transformer lead times ~128 weeks) and community/planning opposition sit between committed capital and earnings.

Cap-rate reversal: FY26 valuation gains were driven by compression (5.08% to 4.96%); a reversal hits Partnership NTA, AUM-based fees and the realisable development margin at once, and the FX hedge (65-90% of net offshore investment) leaves a translation gap on ~56% of the portfolio.
Operating tax rate (9% on post-LTIP EBIT) depends on the trust/company earnings mix and on proposed stapled-structure tax reform; a shift toward taxed development and management income raises it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API, GMG.AX regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 24.56-34.78
data_sources.financials: GMG.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY2016-FY2026, OperatingProfit, ProfitBeforeTax, InterestIncome, DividendsPaid, WeightedAvgSecurities); GMG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt: Analysis of operating profit and reconciliation to statutory profit (lines 896-945), operating-profit definition (669-674), LTIP treatment (1255-1295, 3136-3145), NTA per security 11.79 and 2,044.8m securities (632-635, 3235, 3294), interest-bearing liabilities 6,030.8 (1345), diluted EPS denominator 2,090.0m (9086-9088), lease liabilities 60.2 (11457), NCI 28.5 (14233)
data_sources.qualitative: GMG.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-22); FY26 Annual Report outlook and FY27 guidance (operating EPS +9.0%, DPS 30.0c, WIP to keep rising, majority of data-centre WIP RFS in CY2028)

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 Operating earnings before operating expenses = Property investment 722.1 + Management 690.1 + Development 1,792.2 (FY26 AR, Analysis of operating profit, line 901-905). This is Goodman's own top line for the three earnings streams; it is NOT the statutory revenue line (2,562.7) in the Metrics CSV, which omits the equity-accounted Partnership share of rent and development profit and cannot be reconciled to Operating Profit (2,674.5 > statutory revenue).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 2,044.8m securities on issue at 30 June 2026 + 47.5m dilutive performance rights (FY26 diluted EPS denominator 2,090.0m less basic 2,042.6m, FY26 AR lines 9086-9088). Held FLAT because the LTIP expense is charged in the flows (charge it once). Goodman's own operating-EPS denominator (2,042.6m) includes only rights that have already been tested against hurdles; the diluted count is the wider and more conservative figure.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. The flow being discounted is Operating Profit, which is already AFTER net finance income/(cost) on the balance-sheet borrowings and after the Partnerships' own gearing (Goodman's share of Partnership rent and development profit is equity-accounted, post the funds' interest). Deducting the A$1,949m of balance-sheet net debt (6,030.8 interest-bearing liabilities - 4,081.5 cash, 30 June 2026) on top would charge the debt twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow, never subtract net debt afterwards). total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Gearing 6.5% (FY25 4.3%), A$6.4bn liquidity, 7.5-year weighted debt maturity.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 free cash flow to equity on the model's definition: Operating Profit 2,674.5 less LTIP expense 465.8 less normalised growth reinvestment 1,719.7 (64.3% of Operating Profit = FY27 guided growth 9% / 14% incremental return on retained equity). Actual FY26 retention was larger: Operating Profit 2,674.5 less distributions 611.4 = 2,063.1 retained (77%), so cash FCFE after actual retention was 145.6. The model uses the growth-consistent reinvestment, not the actual, so that the retained cash beyond what the modelled growth needs (it built the A$4.1bn cash pile from the April-2026 bond issues) is not treated as permanently lost. The statutory FreeCashFlow in the CSV (1,881.1) is NOT usable: 'capex' there is corporate PP&E only (39.5), while the real capital deployment runs through investment properties, inventories and Partnership equity.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Operating Profit FY2026 (Goodman's headline measure; +15.7% on FY25 2,311.2; operating EPS 129.9c +10.1%). Statutory profit 2,778.7 (FY25 1,666.4; FY24 -98.9) is dominated by investment-property and derivative fair-value movements and is not used. Note that FY26 development earnings include 733.7 of cumulative valuation gains realised on properties transferred into Partnerships (FY25: 253.3) - Operating Profit ex those realisations FELL 5.7% (1,940.8 vs 2,057.9); the base case takes management's FY27 guidance anyway but this is why the bear weight is above default.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero deducted. Net finance income (operating) of 109.1 (FY25 33.9) sits inside the EBITDA margin: it is the yield on the A$4.1bn of pre-funded development liquidity and will turn to a cost as WIP is drawn, which the margin path reflects. No cash is added to EV and no debt is deducted, so the excluded-income/matching-asset rule is satisfied in the other direction.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR Analysis of operating profit, 'Share based payments expense (465.8) (2025: 356.2)' listed as a reconciling item BELOW Operating Profit (line 929) - i.e. Goodman's Operating Profit EXCLUDES the LTIP charge; the Board's stated offset is to include tested performance rights in the operating-EPS denominator (lines 3136-3145). The house basis charges the full expense in the flows and holds the diluted count flat; the street basis (Goodman's own) adds it back. Cash-settled LTIP payments were 123.4 (FY25 103.8), funded by issuing securities (line 1481-1482).
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY24-FY26 (ShareRepurchases KPI); the flat count is a modelling convention paid for by expensing the LTIP, not by buybacks. Distribution held at 30.0c since FY19.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T06:10:05Z (ASX regular close; Yahoo v8 chart meta; 52-week range 24.56-34.78)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the AUD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest and no net debt is deducted: AUD 10-year government yield ~4.4% (Sept 2026) + 5.5% equity risk premium x beta 1.0 = 9.9%, rounded to 10.0%, the same rate used for CHC.AX on the same day. Goodman's observed beta is above 1 (development-heavy earnings, rate-sensitive valuations) but that cyclicality is charged in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate (owner-fcf.md 7f). One rate across all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost: lease payments sit inside operating expenses; lease liabilities (60.2 at 30 June 2026, FY26 AR line 11457) are immaterial against A$25bn equity and are excluded from debt (which is zero in the model anyway).
inputs.nci_treatment: Operating Profit is stated 'attributable to Securityholders'; non-controlling interests are 28.5 on the balance sheet (FY26 AR line 14233), immaterial. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.tax_note: Income tax expense (operating) FY26 219.3 on operating earnings before tax of 2,893.8 = 7.6% (FY25 175.5/2,486.7 = 7.1%; FY24 169.7/2,219.1 = 7.6%). Low because Goodman Industrial Trust is a flow-through trust; tax arises in the corporate entities that earn management and development income. The engine taxes EBIT after the LTIP charge (2,893.8 - 465.8 = 2,428.0), so the rate is calibrated at 9.0% to reproduce 219.3 on FY0; it drifts to 10% as the taxed development/management mix and Pillar Two take effect.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = Operating earnings (three streams, 3,204.4). ebitda_margin_path = (Operating earnings - operating expenses + net finance income (operating)) / Operating earnings = (3,204.4 - 419.7 + 109.1)/3,204.4 = 90.3% in FY26 (FY25: (2,853.6 - 400.8 + 33.9)/2,853.6 = 87.1%); D&A is inside operating expenses and immaterial (da_pct 0). sbc_pct_path = LTIP expense / Operating earnings (FY26 465.8/3,204.4 = 14.5%; FY25 12.5%). cash_tax_rate_path applies to EBIT after LTIP. capex_pct_path = growth reinvestment of retained Operating Profit = (next year's growth / incremental return on retained equity) x Operating Profit, expressed as % of Operating earnings (Operating Profit is ~83.5% of Operating earnings): base 14% incremental ROE, bull 18%, bear 10% (= cost of equity, retention creates no value). FY16-FY26: Operating Profit rose 1,959.5 on ~9,800 of cumulative retained earnings, ~20% incremental, in a decade of cap-rate compression; FY26 Operating Profit on average book equity was 11.1%. FCF out of the engine is therefore free cash flow to equity after the LTIP charge and after growth reinvestment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Goodman straddles two routing rows (an IAS 40 fair-value property owner via its Partnership co-investments, plus an operating funds-management and development business that is now 77% of Operating earnings). Rather than a sum-of-parts with a separate NTA leg, the group's own single measure, Operating Profit, is projected and capitalised at the AUD cost of equity with net debt held at zero (REIT-row rule), on the component engine so the dashboard reproduces it (CHC.AX precedent, 2026-09-22). Three Goodman-specific choices: (1) the LTIP is charged in the flows because Operating Profit excludes it (house basis) - Goodman's own number is the street basis; (2) reinvestment of retained earnings is charged as capex so the guided 9% growth is paid for; (3) the FY26 base is taken as reported although 733.7 of it is realised prior-year revaluation gains. Sum-of-parts memo: NTA A$11.79/security (FY26, includes the development inventory and Partnership stakes at book, net of debt) + management platform ~330 post-tax post-LTIP at 15x = A$2.4 + development franchise value above inventory book A$2-4 gives A$16-18, bracketing the street base and above the house base, consistent with the LTIP being a real cost the SOTP ignores. Market at 20x FY26 operating EPS and 2.2x NTA is paying for the data-centre pipeline (78% of A$19.7bn WIP, 25% pre-committed, first RFS mostly CY2028) to lease at scale. Statutory FY24 loss (-98.9) was fair-value marks over Operating Profit of 2,049.4 and is not a trend input; the CSV FreeCashFlow series is not used anywhere in the projection.

bear.growth_rationale: FY27 lands below the 9% guidance (H2-weighted realisations slip). Then the speculative book bites: 75% of the A$19.7bn WIP was uncommitted at June 2026, hyperscaler capex cools and community/grid constraints delay projects, so FY28-FY30 development earnings (56% of Operating earnings; 733.7 of FY26 Operating Profit was realised revaluation gains) fall ~30%, performance fees stay at zero, cap rates widen from 4.96% and Partnership transfers stop. Operating earnings trough ~6.5% below FY26 in FY30, then recover at 3% because investor allocations to development-led industrial reset lower. Property investment earnings (95.6% occupancy, 4.0% like-for-like rent growth) hold, which is why the trough is shallow; no solvency question at 6.5% gearing.
bear.margin_rationale: Sticky platform costs (opex rose 4.7% in FY26 on a 12% earnings rise; ~300 staff dedicated to data centres) while earnings fall, and net finance income swings to a cost as gearing rises to carry stuck WIP; margin troughs ~6pp below FY26 and only partly recovers.
bear.sbc_rationale: Lower vesting probability (75% of LTIP hurdles are operating EPS) and a lower security price cut the charge faster than in base.
bear.capex_rationale: Committed WIP funding cannot be cut in FY27-28 (70%, 65% of Operating Profit retained), then new starts pause and retention falls to 30% while the distribution is held; incremental return on retained equity 10% = cost of equity, so retention creates no value. Terminal retention 25% x 10% = 2.5% growth. Expressed on Operating Profit at ~82% of Operating earnings.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 = operating EPS guidance +9.0% (management: H2-weighted on project completions, leasing and asset transfers). Held at 9% through FY29 as the data-centre WIP (first RFS mostly CY2028) converts to development earnings and AUM-driven base fees, then fades 1pp a year to 3% by FY36. No performance-fee spike (management earnings fell 17.6% in FY26 as performance fees dropped) and no repeat of the FY26 scale of realised revaluation gains.
base.margin_rationale: Operating earnings after operating expenses (13.1% of earnings in FY26, 14.0% FY25) and net finance income/(cost). FY26 90.3% was flattered by 109.1 of net finance income on the A$4.1bn bond-funded cash pile; as the A$19.7bn WIP is drawn and gearing rises within the 0-25% range, net finance turns to a cost, so the margin eases to 88% (FY25 comparable 87.1%).
base.sbc_rationale: LTIP expense 14.5% of Operating earnings in FY26 (12.5% FY25). The Board is collapsing the ten-year LTIP into the five-year plan from FY27 (FY26 AR line 216), which reduces the number of overlapping unvested tranches; the charge glides 0.5pp a year to 11%.
base.capex_rationale: Growth reinvestment of retained Operating Profit at a 14% incremental return on retained equity: retention = next year's growth / 14% (FY27-28 64.3%, then 57.1%, 50.0%, 42.9%, 35.7%, 28.6%, 25.0%, 21.4%, 21.4% at terminal so 3% growth is funded) x Operating Profit (~83.5% of Operating earnings). FY27 implies ~1,880 reinvested against ~2,915 of Operating Profit and a ~615 distribution, close to the actual FY26 retention pattern; the 14% sits between FY26 Operating Profit on book equity (11.1%) and the ~20% incremental return of FY16-FY26, a decade that will not repeat its cap-rate compression.

bull.growth_rationale: FY27 beats guidance on earlier asset transfers; the data-centre pipeline leases at scale (TYO05-style 20-year hyperscale leases repeat across the 0.5GW in WIP and the 6.4GW power bank), so FY28-FY30 development earnings step up as CY2028 RFS dates land and AUM-based fees follow; capital Partners keep funding (four new Partnerships, A$3.2bn raised in FY26). Double-digit growth for four years, then a fade to 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Operating leverage on the platform (opex share falls) offsets the swing of net finance income to cost as WIP is drawn.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = next year's growth / 18% incremental return (the FY16-FY26 experience, lightly haircut): 66.7%, 77.8%, 72.2%, 55.6%, 44.4%, 33.3%, 27.8%, 22.2%, 19.4%, 19.4% of Operating Profit (~84% of Operating earnings). Heavy reinvestment in FY28-29 funds the 12-14% growth; terminal retention 19.4% x 18% = 3.5% growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 30%: development is now 56% of Operating earnings and 27% of FY26 Operating Profit was realised prior-year revaluation gains (ex those, Operating Profit fell 5.7%); WIP pre-commitment halved to 25% in a year while WIP grew 53%; the management (annuity) stream fell 17.6%; and management itself says some projects may never proceed and that global data-centre capital needs exceed capital-market capacity. Not higher because the balance sheet (6.5% gearing, A$6.4bn liquidity) and the 95.6%-occupied logistics book make the bear an earnings case, not a solvency case. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (leasing at scale before CY2028 RFS, continued Partner funding, no cap-rate reversal, LTIP moderating) and the FY26 result already prompted investor caution on revenue-recognition timing. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
